computation: Audit base: workstreams/cote16/. Katz–Messing Theorem2(1)–(2) and its proof read from primary pp.76–77, with images visually verified. Their projectors are rational polynomials in Frobenius obtained by coprime characteristic polynomials and Cayley–Hamilton. The source’s inverse-polynomial step is independently checked in proof_checks.md §8.
fate: Katz–Messing1974 Theorem2 settles the precise finite-field case and hence cases descending with their correspondence to finite fields. It does not by itself cover an arbitrary positive-characteristic field with transcendental moduli, prove numerical=homological equivalence, or establish algebraic Lefschetz inverse cycles universally.
fate_date: Katz–Messing manuscript received8August1973; journal publication1974. No earlier first-circulation date for their exact theorem established.
present_status: As of 19 November 2026: Finite-field claim established; the universal general-field extension is not established by the searched sources. The formal conditional Cayley–Hamilton argument remains valid.

his_statement: PropositionA… un sous-schéma fermé Z… pour tout changement de base
statement: For finitely presented f:X→Y with Y nonempty and finitely presented sheafF, after replacingY by a nonempty open there is a finitely presented closedZ⊂Y universally representing the locus where the pullbackF is flat over the new base. On a chosen finite affine cover, the modules are free after any affine base change factoring throughZ.
computation: Audit base: workstreams/cotes44_47_54/. computations.md §6 reconstructs the noetherian proof: after reduction F_i/IF_i is free; lift a basis, form the ideal of coefficients of all relations, and use nilpotent flatness to show it universally represents freeness/flatness. Sum the finitely many chart ideals. Finite generation follows over the noetherian approximating ring.
fate: EGA IV₃ Proposition11.4.5, pp146–147, is the precise universal closed flattening stratum, including simultaneous freeness on the chosen finite affine cover. The published theorem assumes Y irreducible; the manuscript says merely nonempty. Its broader nonempty version follows by finite-presentation approximation to an affine noetherian base and restriction to a nonempty open contained in one irreducible component; injectivity of the approximating subring map ensures that open has nonempty inverse image. This extension is our explicit argument. Missing4.1bis is EGA IV₃ Cor11.4.4, pp145–146, not a generic definition of flattening.
fate_date: EGA IV₃ received15November1964; published1966; source sheet undated.
present_status: As of 19 November 2026: published irreducible-base result exactly located; source’s nonempty extension verified by the stated approximation argument.

statement: For a locally finite affine-hyperplane arrangement in a finite-dimensional real affine space, a chamber is the intersection of its wall half-spaces; every hyperplane supports adjacent chambers; the relative interior of a given wall is a chamber of the induced arrangement and has one uniquely determined adjacent chamber on the opposite side.

A compact segment meets finitely many hyperplanes; at a point on just one wall a ball is cut into exactly two components; connectedness of the wall interior propagates the adjacent chamber.
fate: The content is standard chamber geometry, consistent with the root/chamber framework in SGA3XXI §§3, 5. Searches for the exact French phrase, number391 and Bourbaki context did not identify the originating typescript. The mathematical result is checked independently, but source authorship and exact publication are not assigned.
